2. My partner is vegetarian: no meat, no fish. Eggs and dairy are fine. No allergies.
3. We like pasta, rice bowls and soups. No other strong preferences.
4. Friday is takeout, so Saturday to Thursday.
5. Monday to Thursday, dinner has to be on the table within 25 minutes. Weekends, up to an hour is fine.
6. Cheap-ish, nothing fancy.
7. No strong preference.
8. A two-burner stove and a microwave. No oven, no air fryer, no slow cooker, no pressure cooker.
9. Friday is takeout.
output:
Great, this is enough to work with. Quick note on your setup: everything below is vegetarian by default (since your partner doesn't eat meat/fish and it's easiest to cook one pot for all three of you on two burners). If you want meat in your own portion some nights, I've flagged easy no-extra-pot ways to add it. Let me know if you'd rather I build meat into the base recipes instead.

## Saturday (up to 1 hr) — Soup
**Vegetable & White Bean Minestrone + Grilled Cheese**
- Sauté onion, carrot, celery, garlic in olive oil.
- Add canned diced tomatoes, veggie broth, canned white beans, small pasta (ditalini/elbow), simmer 15–20 min. Season mild (no chili flakes).
- Toss in a handful of spinach at the end.
- Serve with grilled cheese sandwiches (stovetop, second burner or after soup simmers).
- *Add meat option:* pan-sear diced ham or Italian sausage separately, stir into your own bowl.

## Sunday (up to 1 hr) — Pasta
**Skillet "Baked" Ziti**
- Boil pasta (penne/ziti) in one pot.
- In the other pan, simmer marinara sauce with a big spoonful of ricotta stirred in.
- Combine pasta + sauce in the pan, top with shredded mozzarella, cover on low heat 5 min until melted.
- *Add meat option:* brown ground beef or Italian sausage in the sauce pan before adding marinara (for your portion, cook a small separate batch or the whole batch if your family eats meat sauce Sundays and partner has a veggie-only scoop set aside first).

## Monday (25 min) — Rice Bowl
**Veggie Fried Rice**
- Use pre-cooked/day-old rice (or microwave-in-bag rice for speed).
- One pan: scramble eggs, set aside. Same pan: stir-fry frozen peas/carrots/corn, garlic, splash of soy sauce.
- Add rice, eggs back in, toss, mild soy/sesame oil seasoning (no chili).
- *Add meat option:* quickly stir-fry diced chicken or shrimp first, remove, set aside, add back to your bowl at the end.

## Tuesday (25 min) — Pasta
**Simple Tomato Butter Pasta**
- Boil pasta.
- Meanwhile, melt butter with garlic, canned crushed tomatoes, pinch of sugar, simmer while pasta cooks.
- Toss together, top with parmesan and fresh basil if you have it.
- *Add meat option:* stir in pre-cooked rotisserie chicken pieces or browned Italian sausage at the end for your serving.

## Wednesday (25 min) — Soup
**Quick Lentil & Spinach Soup**
- Use canned lentils to save time.
- Sauté onion/garlic, add veggie broth, canned lentils, canned diced tomatoes, cumin (mild), simmer 10 min.
- Stir in spinach at the end, serve with bread/crackers.
- *Add meat option:* add sliced kielbasa or diced ham while simmering (separately for your bowl if partner wants meat-free).

## Thursday (25 min) — Rice Bowl
**Black Bean & Cheese Rice Bowls**
- Microwave rice.
- One pan: warm canned black beans with corn, cumin, lime juice (mild, no heat).
- Build bowls: rice, beans/corn, shredded cheese, sour cream, avocado if you have it.
- *Add meat option:* quickly pan-sear diced chicken or ground beef with the same mild seasoning, serve on the side.

---

**Notes:**
- All recipes avoid spice/heat for your 6-year-old — you can add hot sauce or chili flakes to individual adult bowls if you want more kick.
- Ingredients lean on pantry staples (canned beans/tomatoes, pasta, rice, frozen veg) to keep costs down.
- Want me to turn this into a consolidated shopping list too?
